M-CODE-GRAPH.NAME: Octocode code-graph adapter
M-CODE-GRAPH.purpose: Read real file-level import edges and per-file symbols from a running Octocode MCP server in a short-lived, read-only session (ADR-9), so impact/trace can be enriched without making the core gates depend on it.

export-READ_ONLY_TOOLS.PURPOSE: ADR-9 allowlist of MCP tools this adapter may call: graphrag, view_signatures, structural_search.

export-collectImportEdges.PURPOSE: One MCP session; graphrag get-relationships per supplied file; deduped, sorted imports edges; missing/broken tools → available:false + notes.

export-collectFileSymbols.PURPOSE: One view_signatures call; per-file deduped symbol names/kinds; requested files always present.

export-parseGraphRelationships.PURPOSE: Defensive parser for recorded payloads: plain file endpoints only, imports only, dedupe/sort; invalid JSON → INTEGRATION_INVALID_OUTPUT note.

export-parseViewSignatures.PURPOSE: Defensive parser for signatures payloads; symbol endpoints with kinds; dedupe per file.

CrossLink.relation: resolution, kill switch, pinned range and scrubbed child env come from ADR-9 registry
impact --code-graph maps edges to module DEPENDS and emits CODE_EDGE_UNDECLARED / DECLARED_EDGE_UNUSED
trace --code compares MODULE_MAP names with real symbols (CONTRACT_SYMBOL_MISSING)

contract.purpose: Answer two read-only questions about real code: which module files import which, and which symbols a file exports.

param.name: root
param.description: Project root; also the MCP server --path and worker cwd.

param.name: config
param.description: Supplies integrations.octocode bin/timeout and the tested range.

param.name: files
param.description: Module source files (project-relative or absolute inside root); paths outside the root are rejected.

param.name: graph
param.description: { available, version, edges[], notes[] } — notes carry INTEGRATION_* degradation codes.

error.description: Tool missing/disabled/unsupported or MCP session failed — available:false, command continues with its deterministic output.
Session or per-call timeout — note only; never a crash.
Malformed JSON or unexpected tool payload — note only; never executed as code.

notes.note-1: Read-only MCP tools only; no index, no semantic embeddings, no LLM, no network (graph/structural mode is tree-sitter over current sources).
notes.note-2: Session lifecycle: spawn octocode mcp --path <root>, initialize, optional tools/list sanity check, calls, close in finally; one session per command invocation.
notes.note-3: Honest limitation (v1.4.0): the pinned Octocode 0.29.2 Linux binary did not answer MCP initialize on our dev host; the contract is proven with recorded payloads and a fake MCP server, and the real-binary smoke is manual (`bun run test:integrations --download`).
notes.note-4: External output is untrusted data: parsed defensively, capped (4 MB/tool, 12 notes), never shell-interpolated.
